newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Adecco posts 1996 proforma gain, net loss.
newsitem.headline: Adecco posts 1996 proforma gain, net loss.

text.p: Swiss-French temporary employment firm Adecco SA said its proforma net profit for 1996 was 241 million Swiss francs, an increase of 17 percent versus 206 million francs for 1995.
Adecco reported a net loss of 11.1 million in the year ending December 31, 1996, after goodwill amortisation and merger-related costs. Revenues were 6.386 billion francs.

Adecco was reporting a proforma figure after being formed last year by a merger of Swiss-based Adia and French concern Ecco. The merger created a temporary employment giant rivalling U.S. firm Manpower Inc.

The net loss figure of 11.1 million Swiss francs followed charges for goodwill amortisation of 191.8 million francs and merger-related restructuring costs of 21.3 million, Adecco said in a statement released before a news conference.
Adecco chief executive John Bowmer said that recent results showed an accelerating trend in revenues which "shows every sign of continuing well into 1997".
"As a result of this strong performance, the executive committee will recommend to the board of directors and the general assembly a dividend of five Swiss francs per bearer share," Bowmer said.
Operations in France were also showing growth again this year, he said in a speech released before the news conference.
